A government report page whose body is a review table with MULTI-LINE cells — the hardest ordering case in the set, and deliberately the opposite of arxiv_gpt3 p7. There the cells are single-line, so the table reads row-wise; here each cell wraps over up to ten lines, so reading row-wise shreds every sentence and the correct order is cell by cell. A tool cannot get both right from geometry alone without knowing where the cell boundaries are, which is what a table model provides.

Columns: Review Type (x=162), Performer (x=321), Date of Review (x=443), Purpose (x=537), Outcome (x=978). The 'Date of Review' header itself wraps (3 at y=281, 8 at y=305) and straddles the other headers at y=293, so even the header row is not a single baseline.

Expect Docyx to score poorly here. That is the point of the page: the truth set previously contained no case that the geometry cannot reach.
